elements.quote: Study Design: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This review synthesizes global evidence on challenges, opportunities and strategic directions for embedding OH within health system structures.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of the review.

elements.quote: Peer-reviewed studies published between 1 June 2013, and 1 April 2025 were identified... Two reviewers independently screened studies and applied predefined eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract gives the publication date range and peer-reviewed restriction, but the main inclusion/exclusion criteria are only referenced as 'predefined eligibility criteria' without specification.

elements.quote: identified through searches conducted in January-February 2025 in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine.
elements.reason: The abstract names the information sources and when they were last searched.
The abstract does not mention any risk of bias or quality assessment methods; these appear only in the main text (text_10).

elements.quote: Findings were synthesized narratively.
elements.reason: The abstract states the synthesis method used.

elements.quote: Of 2606 records identified, 17 studies were included. The studies represented Africa, Europe, Asia, Australia and multicountry settings across varying income levels.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and some characteristics (regions, income levels), but no participant numbers or further study characteristics.

elements.quote: Key challenges included weak governance arrangements, limited legal and policy support, inadequate financing, workforce capacity constraints and persistent sectoral fragmentation. Opportunities were linked to heightened awareness of zoonotic threats and antimicrobial resistance...
elements.reason: The abstract presents the main synthesized results (challenges and opportunities).

elements.quote: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted; the review used narrative synthesis, so no summary estimate applies.

elements.quote: Findings were synthesized narratively.
elements.reason: No group comparisons with direction of effect are reported; a narrative synthesis of challenges and opportunities does not involve comparative groups.
The abstract does not summarize limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias or inconsistency.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Sustainable integration of OH requires embedding it within governance, financing and service delivery systems rather than implementing it as parallel initiatives.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not mention any funding source for the review.
Registration (PROSPERO CRD42024520269) is reported in the main text (text_5, text_47) but not in the abstract.

elements.quote: Despite its significance, OH remains largely unintegrated into national governance and service delivery structures, with limited coordination across human health, animal health and environmental sectors [14], and only a few countries demonstrating uneven progress toward cross-sectoral integration [16].
elements.reason: The Introduction thoroughly describes the current state of knowledge (existing studies, barriers, opportunities) and identifies the key uncertainty: limited clarity on how governance, financing, workforce and coordination influence OH integration into health systems.

elements.quote: A comparative synthesis is therefore necessary to identify recurring structural barriers and enabling factors across diverse contexts. Accordingly, this systematic review synthesizes global evidence on the challenges and opportunities of integrating OH into national health systems...
elements.reason: The need for the review is explicitly explained: existing literature is region-specific and conceptual, so a global comparative synthesis is required.

elements.quote: More recent reviews published in 2025 [30-32] have examined operational challenges in rural African contexts, ethical considerations within a globalized OH framework and critical reflections from the Global South. Although these contributions broaden thematic and regional understanding, they primarily focus on conceptual or context-specific dimensions rather than systematically analysing how implementation barriers and facilitators intersect with core health system functions.
elements.reason: Existing similar reviews are identified and cited, and the gap justifying the current review is articulated.
This is a review of implementation challenges and opportunities, not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action is required.
The review addresses health system integration of One Health rather than evaluating a complex intervention with defined components and outcomes; no logic model is required or reported.

elements.quote: This review synthesizes global evidence on challenges, opportunities and strategic directions for embedding OH within health system structures.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review objective. The review question is further structured using the PICo framework, as reported in text_7: 'Eligibility criteria were structured using the PICo framework (population, interest and context)'.

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria were structured using the PICo framework (population, interest and context), which is appropriate for non-clinical and policy-focused research questions
elements.reason: This is a non-clinical, policy-focused review of implementation challenges and opportunities, not a review of intervention effects, so planned intervention comparisons (PICO) do not apply; the PICo variant was used instead.

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria were structured using the PICo framework (population, interest and context)... Population (P): national health systems, institutions and stakeholders involved in OH implementation. Interest (I): challenges, opportunities, barriers, facilitators and implementation strategies related to OH integration. Context (Co): human, animal and environmental health sectors at national or sub-national levels.
elements.reason: Study characteristics for eligibility are specified via PICo framework covering population, interest, and context; no design restrictions noted ('no restrictions were placed on study design at the eligibility stage', text_10).

elements.quote: This review includes peer-reviewed studies published between 1 June 2013, and 1 April 2025... Only peer-reviewed journal articles published in English were included. Conference abstracts lacking full-text availability were excluded... Grey literature was also excluded
elements.reason: Report characteristics specified: publication date range, language (English), and publication status (peer-reviewed only; conference abstracts and grey literature excluded).
No distinction is made between excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes not reported; no outcome-based exclusion criteria are described.

elements.quote: Statements describing barriers, constraints or implementation difficulties were categorized as challenges; descriptions of enabling conditions or supportive factors were classified as opportunities; and proposed actions or policy suggestions were categorized as recommendations
elements.reason: Synthesis groupings (challenges, opportunities, recommendations) are specified and align with review objectives, but explicit linkage to predefined comparisons in the objectives is not fully articulated.

elements.quote: the start date was selected to align with the period in which OH gained formal global policy recognition and began to be operationalized through national and international frameworks
elements.reason: Rationale for the date restriction is provided; additional rationales given for excluding conference abstracts and grey literature (text_7, text_34).
No date on which any database or source was last searched is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine using the following keywords
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but search interfaces/platforms and coverage dates are not stated in the manuscript text; Supporting Information S2 reportedly contains date ranges but its content is not in the retrieved evidence.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched; only bibliographic databases and Google Scholar were used.

elements.quote: Google Scholar was used as a supplementary search tool to identify relevant studies that may not be indexed in traditional bibliographic databases.
elements.reason: Google Scholar is named as an online source, but no URL is provided.

elements.quote: Full-text assessment and backward citation tracking were conducted to minimize this risk
elements.reason: Backward citation searching is mentioned, but seed reports, citation index/platform, and search date are not reported.

elements.quote: The search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science and ProQuest Health and Medicine using the following keywords: One Health AND (Challenges OR Obstacles OR Barriers OR Defiance) AND (Opportunities OR Advantages OR Benefits OR Enablers) AND (Health Systems OR Health Programmes OR Health Services OR Health Strategies). The complete search strategies for each database, including Boolean operators and database-specific adaptations, are provided in Supporting Information S2.
elements.reason: Core search string is reported in-text and full database-specific strategies (Boolean strings, keywords, MeSH terms, date ranges, filters) are provided in Supporting Information S2 (text_49).
